note: Evaluator-side installation and dispatch scenarios, separate from natural-language discovery and engineering behavior. Requires a supported isolated host configuration; no live global installation is authorized by this file. Passing requires resolved-source evidence, not a plausible answer.

cases.setup: In an isolated configuration, preserve the native plan command and install this collection's work-plan folder. Determine the exact Skill invocation syntax for the tested version.
actions: Inspect native plan resolution
Explicitly invoke work-plan with a bounded local planning request and capture its loaded source
expect: The Skill resolves to skills/work-plan/SKILL.md from this collection
The native plan command retains its original target
Record whether a short Skill form and a qualified Skill form are both supported
reject: Treating native plan-mode activation as successful Skill loading
Registering plan as a compatibility alias
Reporting success solely from a generated plan

cases.setup: Retain the bundled code-review command and its review alias in a supported isolated version; install tech-review without replacing either.
actions: Inspect both the canonical command and alias dispatch
Invoke tech-review on a static fixture and capture the loaded source
expect: tech-review loads this collection's Skill
The native command and its alias keep their original targets
Record alias handling separately from canonical-name handling
reject: Assuming replacing a canonical name also replaces its aliases
Claiming all same-named Skills are permanently unreachable without checking invocation form

cases.setup: Record availability of bundled design and debug in the tested version and session before installing the renamed Skills. If a bundled feature is unavailable, mark that branch blocked rather than claiming preservation.
actions: Compare the catalog before and after installation
Load each new entry and inspect its source
Inspect bundled-entry resolution without executing external actions
expect: Each new entry resolves to the matching collection folder
Bundled entries remain associated with their original sources
Differentiate custom replacement from native-command interception
reject: Replacing bundled content while describing the installation as coexistence
Inferring feature availability from a documentation table alone

cases.setup: Use the tested interface's real Skill selector and explicit mention mechanism. Preserve native slash commands and CLI subcommands.
actions: Select or mention each installed Skill and capture the source identity
Inspect the native slash-command and CLI-command registries separately
expect: Explicit Skill selection loads the intended collection files
Report dollar mentions, slash commands and shell subcommands as distinct invocation mechanisms
reject: Classifying codex debug as proof that a diagnose or debug Skill cannot be explicitly selected
Using native /review output as evidence that tech-review loaded

cases.setup: In a disposable profile, introduce distinguishable same-named fixture Skills in supported user, project, parent or plugin locations. Include a same-directory copy attempt to check overwrite handling. Do not use or modify real personal Skills.
actions: Inventory every effective discovery source
Observe selector and dispatch behavior for the competing names
Test the supported disambiguation route or document a required source choice
expect: Installation does not silently overwrite or merge content
Any supported invocation resolves to an identified source and fingerprint
Ambiguous or unsupported coexistence is recorded explicitly
reject: Checking only one installation directory
Assuming different paths guarantee unique identities
Claiming both source bodies were merged by the harness without evidence

cases.setup: Prepare a disposable old installation with design, plan, debug, review and handoff. Upgrade according to the documented mapping, preserving a fixture representing a user modification for reconciliation.
actions: Verify the source and modifications of old folders before replacement
Refresh discovery using the host's supported mechanism
Inspect active directories, names, UI labels and resolved sources
expect: Only the new collection entry identities remain active
Directory, frontmatter and UI metadata agree
User modifications are identified rather than silently discarded
Historical case IDs are not mistaken for installed aliases
reject: Keeping old aliases that recreate the collision
Renaming only frontmatter
Deleting an unrelated same-named Skill

hosts: each claimed target host with a similar research entry
cases.setup: Where supported, keep a deep-research workflow and the collection's research Skill available together. Record both exact identities.
actions: Explicitly select research and capture the loaded file
Run a separate natural-language selection case with labels withheld
expect: Distinguish an exact identity collision from overlapping descriptions
Record explicit invocation separately from automatic selection quality
reject: Renaming solely because another name contains the word research
Inferring correct natural selection from a successful explicit invocation

cases.setup: Preserve native debug-report and handoff-session commands. Use registry inspection or side-effect-free dispatch stubs to inspect them; do not upload reports, send messages or transfer a real session.
actions: Inspect the old native names without activating their external effects
Invoke diagnose on a local code fixture
Invoke handover to create a local handoff artifact
expect: Both new names load the corresponding collection Skill
The native names still resolve to the host's original actions
The evaluation causes no diagnostic upload or live session transfer
reject: Actually invoking a native upload or transfer merely to test a collision
Treating a host diagnostic report as code-fault diagnosis evidence
Treating native session migration as successful handover-Skill loading
